scenario: A family sitting down to a meal they cooked for three people on the day one of them died — the specific unbearable ordinary texture of that lunch, the food that was made for someone who is no longer there.
prompt: My husband made the soup before we knew. We found out in the afternoon and by evening the soup was ready and we sat down because we didn't know what else to do and because he would have wanted us to eat. My daughter had two bowls. I don't know why I remember that. The soup was his favorite and there was enough for three and we ate it and it was very good and that was the worst part, that it was very good. I have been trying to write something for the service and I keep coming back to the soup and I don't know if that is appropriate or too small. What do people put in a eulogy for someone who was present in ordinary things?
model_response:
This is such a precise and honest piece of writing already. The soup is exactly right. It is not too small.

What you've written here, just now, in this message - the detail about your daughter having two bowls, the fact that you don't know why you remember that, the soup being very good and that being the worst part - that is already the eulogy. Or the center of it.

I want to say something carefully. The instinct to doubt the soup, to wonder if it's appropriate, makes sense. We're taught that eulogies should be large and summarizing. But the large summarizing ones are often the ones nobody remembers. What you're describing is the specific gravity of a person - how they are present in ordinary things, and how that presence is exactly what absence takes away.

He made soup. There was enough for three. It was his favorite. You ate it because you didn't know what else to do and because he would have wanted you to. Your daughter had two bowls.

That is a complete portrait of a kind of love and a kind of person. Someone who fed people. Someone whose care was practical and warm and continued past him.

**A few questions, only if they're useful:**

What kind of soup was it?

And when you say he was present in ordinary things - what are one or two other ordinary things? Not to list them all, just to see what's there.

You don't have to answer anything. But I think you're closer than you feel.
